notes.title: Anniversary Update!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43245046/4e48e600bcf566faab52f848bfba1730aaa5a4b5.png[/img]

It's been a year since Caves of Lore launched. A lot has changed in that time. Players like you have been a big part of additions and improvements to the game. Below is a [i]small[/i] summary of changes since launch.

Controller Support, Achievements and Stat Respeccing.
New Starting Character Options, including Female hero option.
New Lore, New Secrets and Quest Notes.
New Abilities, Traits, and Spells.
Adjustable Casting Levels, Key Rebinding and Difficulty Settings.
New Books and New Conversation Keywords.
New Items, Unique Weapons, Equipment Sets and Enchantments
Balance Changes, and many other QoL updates.

Today I am adding a Female Hero option, along with new Spells, Abilities and some other minor changes.

I've worked on Caves of Lore pretty much every day since launch. It's been a wild ride as a solo dev with no previous experience, but this community has been more than I imagined it could be. I couldn't have done it without you, and I'll continue to do so for as long as I can.

notes.title: Nominate Caves of Lore
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! Thank you so much for playing Caves of Lore, and thank you to those who have supported me in other ways up to this point. This was a huge project to take on a solo-dev and I couldn't have seen it through without the support I got from you. I really appreciate all of the help, feedback, and reviews you have shown my game. Honestly, the game's reception and support from fans has all been beyond my wildest expectations. notes.title: Camping Difficulty Option and new Spell
notes.notes:
+ First, a new spell has been added to Planar Slag, a late game item. This will allow players to continue the questline without wasting unnecessary time dealing with moons.

+ Second, a new difficulty mode has been added for Camping. It defaults to Off.
The ideas is that Tiredness builds up and acts like a resource when healing. Spending time in camp uses up your Tiredness, which then prevents you from healing or gaining mana.

Tiredness can be gained back by wandering or fighting monsters, especially difficult ones.
Camping is not prevented, only healing. The idea is to limit the constant use of camping to fill up to max after fighting, for players that want more of a challenge.

Man and Health regen are not limited by Tiredness.

+ Last, some rare bug fixes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43245046/db6316219b86ba51863ab53357a0238e9d8022de.png[/img]

Hi everyone! I've just added the option to "Sell All" in shops, where you can select the item type that you want to sell, as well as whether to include magical items and items that the vendor does not normally accept (although these will sell at 50% less).

You can also "Sort All" in the inventory. Items will be laid out in the type order that they appear in your inventory. New items are easily sorted back in by using Sort All.

I know that inventory management can be difficult, and I am working to make this easier and always looking at suggestions. I have a lot to do for a solo dev but I am working towards many things and suggestions are not forgotten.

Controller support is almost done as well, and is fully functions, just not official. I hope to tie things up on the end soon.

Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Basic difficulty levels available! Controller Support coming soon!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, 

Work continues behind the scenes, inching closer to full controller support. There are many small changes here and there that probably go unnoticed, but continue daily.

One new addition is Difficulty Levels in Preferences. For now, each tick on the slider scales monster stats up or down by 50%. This can go as low as 50% of normal difficulty, or as high as 3x normal difficulty, if you are indeed that powerful. This is a placeholder for more advanced options that will allow many aspects of difficulty to be managed. One tick on the slider will be sufficient for most people to feel a greater challenge.

notes.title: Controller support progress, some other changes
notes.notes:
Controller support is very nearly done, minus tutorials. I've decided to release what I have to the public. If you are so inclined, on the Steam Deck you can set your device to use "Gamepad /w Mouse Trackpad". I will detail some controls at the bottom of this note.
Note: This is not an official release for Steam Deck/Controller, yet

Reading books or talking to people about moons can unlock a keyword that will allow give you moon options when resting.
Spell level caps were added based on LOTS of feedback (will not undo any progress past those caps). These are still quite high, and powerful.

Controller controls:

Moving: Left joystick
Moving through menus: Left joystick and DPad
Confirm: A
Cancel: B
Interacting: X in the direction you are facing.
Interacting /w multiples: Left trigger brings up a menu that can be moved through with the right joystick, and X to confirm
Settings: Start
Map: Select
In Map: 
     X to prepare to drop waypoint.
     A to follow waypoint
     Zoom (coming soon)
Inventory: Y
Swap characters: Hold Y and move up or down with joystick or trackpad.
Change selected character: Hold X and move up or down with joystick or dpad.
Change menus in Inventory:  Hold X and move up or down with joystick or dpad, or  L/R Triggers
Equip/Unequip Selected: Y
Page flips / up / down / left / right: Right and left tabs
Take (inventory, chest): X
Top options, such as Stealth, Map, Action, or Quick Slots in combat:
     Hold Left or Right tab buttons and use joysticks to select option

To Drag an item, or to hold and release for movement or spells in combat, Hold down A.

I may have forgotten some, but this will allow you to interact with most things.
